description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md "not low-hanging" table (it needs a ruling, so it is not on THE LIST).  Code sha 05806e16.

THE POLICY: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-compile-module-p` -- unset PCL_COMPILE_DIRS means perl's installed library directories + PCL's own lib/ (the trust class :installed); a module anywhere else is :local and loads from the cached .lisp text.  Ruled s471 (Fable; DECIDED lines 2608 / 2687): "a module under -I/PERL5LIB/. is probably being EDITED, and a fasl is the most opaque artifact PCL writes"; the main script was exempted for exactly this cost (#1841: "3.3 s of the 5.6 s").  Correctness is the dependency manifest either way ("this is a belt", DECIDED 2687) -- the fasl is keyed on the source content like the text.

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/lm/: Text::Balanced copied as My::TB under a `use lib` dir, a 2-line program using it; warm, best of 5, legs/leg1.log, load 1.1): default 0.530 s; PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*' 0.055 s; perl 0.009 s.  So ~0.2 s per 1,000 lines of local module, on EVERY run -- an application with its own lib/ tree of 10,000 lines pays ~2 s per invocation that a fasl would not.

THE QUESTION FOR THE USER (or the reviewing session): flip the default to "compile everything" now that the manifest guards staleness (keeping PCL_NO_COMPILE_DIRS for the edit-loop case), or compile a :local module once its source has been UNCHANGED for N runs, or keep the ruling.  The implementation is a one-line default either way; the decision is the opacity argument vs ~0.2 s per 1,000 lines per run.

ALSO SEEN (separate task #4987): a program that uses the VENDORED PPI as a library rebuilds it on every run even with PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*'.

=== INPUT (s540b, leg3) === the SBCL compile of that text is policy-sensitive: compile-file of five emitted units at (speed 1) (compilation-speed 2) (space 1) instead of the generated code's (speed 2) (safety 1) (debug 0) takes JSON::PP 1.16 -> 0.55 s, Text::Balanced 0.81 -> 0.37, Math::BigInt::Calc 3.07 -> 1.05, Pod::Simple::BlackBox 4.03 -> 0.72 (legs/leg3.log, comp/comp-leg.pl) -- a THIRD option for a :local module (compile it cheaply, or fasl it) besides flipping the default; the RUN-time cost of the cheaper policy was NOT measured (that is the next measurement, on the bench rows that load a module).

=== RULED (the USER, s540, 2026-11-13) === the default CHANGES: a local module is compiled once and its compiled file reused, like an installed module.  Staleness is guarded by the content manifest and TESTED (five shapes) in the batch that builds it: s540/s540d-prompt.md member 5.  PCL_NO_COMPILE_DIRS stays the opt-out.  DECIDED ## s540.
subject: DECISION ASKED (s540b, measured): a program's OWN modules (under `use lib` / -I / PERL5LIB / `.`) are never compiled to a fasl by default -- their cached Lisp TEXT is compiled by SBCL on EVERY run: one 2,400-line local module costs 0.53 s per run against 0.055 s with PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*' (perl 0.009 s)
